body:
## Relationships

- Parent and close gate: #38
- Blocked by: #32, canonical temporal columns/indexes, and the temporal controller
- Related: #35 layout scheduling and #36 interaction
- Blocks: #38

## Problem

GraphForge graphs need valid-time and event-time exploration without rebuilding graphs, losing UUID identity, or racing layout and interaction work.

## Objective

Bind canonical node/edge time columns to graph projections and provide a scale-aware graph timebar and playback path.

## Requirements

- Bind valid-from, valid-to, and event-at columns to canonical node/edge UUID identity.
- Apply Rust-produced visibility bitsets before graph LOD, layout updates, picking, styling, and geographic LOD.
- Preserve selection, focus, pinned state, aggregate membership, and provenance across frames.
- Never rebuild or mutate the canonical source graph for a time change.
- Integrate timebar scrub/step/play/pause with cancellable worker layout and stale-reply rejection.
- Define static-export freezing for cursor/range/window/timezone and visible identity membership.
- Emit bounded diagnostics for invalid bindings, over-budget filters, and cancelled work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GraphForge assertion-validity and event-history fixtures produce correct frame membership at every half-open boundary.
- Selection and UUID provenance remain stable while elements enter and leave visibility.
- Rapid scrub/play/dispose cannot apply stale visibility or layout updates.
- Direct and aggregate LOD tiers report exact deterministic membership.
- Frozen HTML/PNG/SVG exports identify temporal state and visible membership.

## BDD Completion Scenarios

### Scenario: Analyst scrubs valid-time graph state

Given a graph with node and edge validity intervals
When the analyst scrubs across an interval boundary
Then only currently valid identities are visible
And the underlying projection, selection, and provenance remain unchanged.

### Scenario: Playback cannot race disposal

Given active temporal playback and progressive layout
When a newer revision arrives or the view closes
Then older filter/layout replies are rejected
And all owned work is cancelled.

## Testing

Graph validity boundary goldens; source immutability; selection/provenance stability; worker race and cancellation tests; direct/aggregate LOD membership; frozen export; large/massive playback evidence.

## Documentation

Update graph-temporal binding, worker lifecycle, LOD ordering, export, diagnostics, and examples.

## Non-Goals

- Generic transition animation.
- Inferring temporal fields from GraphForge results.

## Rust/WASM Architecture Amendment

- Visibility, identity membership, temporal-before-graph/geographic LOD ordering, and frozen export state are Rust-owned and equivalent in native and WASM execution.
- Browser timebar and playback controls submit revisioned commands to the WASM Worker; they do not rebuild or filter graph topology in TypeScript.
- Add native-versus-WASM time-filtered graph scene, selection, cancellation, and export parity.

This section is authoritative over any earlier host-ownership wording in this issue. It does not broaden third-party payload compatibility or legacy-reader scope.

## Verification

Follow #108's shared lean CI policy: bounded correctness and affected integration checks in the existing Release surfaces aggregate; hosted performance/100M+ runs scheduled/manual, full platform evidence at release. Reuse hash-linked evidence; no duplicate gate or repeated-green-run requirement.
title: Add temporal graph bindings, timebar playback, and identity-safe filtering
